earlier_issuances.narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast
Daytime highs reaching 31.5°C / 89°F under mostly cloudy skies early, turning overcast by midday and back to mostly cloudy by evening. Winds develop from the southwest by midday, with peak gusts ashore reaching 36 km/h (19 kt). Thunder possible, peaking this evening. Overnight temperatures drop to a low of 20.5°C / 69°F. Solar UV index reaches a peak of 8.6 today, requiring protection during midday hours. Air quality across ground sensors ranges from an AQI of 12 to 71, with the highest reading at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, while model guidance estimates overall US AQI near 82.

## Extended Outlook
Temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with showers possible Friday and thunderstorms likely each day. Wednesday and Thursday will bring partly cloudy skies, with daytime highs on Friday spanning a range of 28.1°C / 83°F to 33.3°C / 92°F under mostly cloudy conditions, accompanied by a 65% chance of rain. Looking further into the extended period from Saturday through Tuesday, partly cloudy conditions prevail Saturday to Monday before returning to mostly cloudy skies on Tuesday. Rain probability rises to 80% by Tuesday as convective activity remains active across the basin.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability builds significantly across the basin today, though model estimates diverge widely on its intensity. GFS projects minimal instability with peak CAPE of only 270 J/kg, whereas ECMWF (2640 J/kg), ICON (2960 J/kg), and UKMO (3550 J/kg) all indicate moderate to strong instability peaking around 18:00. Any developing thunderstorm can produce violent, sudden downdraft gusts well above daily background winds. Boaters and outdoor recreationalists should remain vigilant for rapid cloud build-up and localized strong winds during the late afternoon and evening hours.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Over Winam Gulf, winds start overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), then into the evening at 11 km/h (6 kt) gusting 22 km/h (12 kt). Peak gusts over open waters are expected to reach 29.7 km/h (16 kt). With convective instability present across the lake basin this evening, sudden thunder squalls and hazardous localized downdraft gusts remain the primary safety risk for marine craft.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1017 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Across the Nyanza Basin, mean sea level pressure spans from 1012.3 hPa near Kisumu to 1014.5 hPa in the southern highlands. A gradual 24-72 hour falling pressure trend across regional points will maintain persistent low-level convergence and support renewed afternoon and evening convection along the lake-land interface.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
The guidance behind this issuance is at least 9 hours old (models last aligned at 18:00Z). In long-run verification, ECMWF is established as the most reliable rain caller at Day+0, whereas GFS and Kenya Met exhibit lower hit rates. Yesterday's target date saw GFS and UKMO correctly verify dry conditions, while ECMWF and ICON over-predicted rain. Standing bias checks highlight that GFS and UKMO consistently under-forecast peak gust speeds, justifying the upward bias calibration of primary peak wind to 36.0 km/h (19 kt). Note that the local bulletin from the Kenya Meteorological Department was unavailable this cycle due to a fetch connection timeout. Individual ground air quality stations reported as follows: Kisumu Airport at AQI 12 (PM2.5 12.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central at AQI 71 (PM2.5 71.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach at AQI 53 (PM2.5 53.0 µg/m³).
